slides.title: Dozens of Sessions, One Person
bullets: A large congress can run dozens or even hundreds of simultaneous sessions
No single MSL can attend everything
Session tracking turns that limit into strategic coverage instead of random attendance

slides.title: Prioritize Before the Congress Starts
bullets: Must-attend: anything on your product, its comparator, or a priority KOL talk
High-value but optional: sessions on emerging therapeutic-area trends
Coverable without attending: via a teammate's summary or the published abstract

slides.title: Coordinate Coverage as a Team
bullets: Relevant session volume often exceeds what one MSL can cover
Split key sessions among the MSLs present on site
Assign someone to take structured notes on each one
Consolidate everything into a shared repository to avoid gaps and overlap

slides.title: What Structured Notes Actually Capture
bullets: The core scientific message of the talk
Concrete data: effect size, population studied, comparator
Methodological limitations raised by the speaker or the Q&A
Audience reaction, and any direct implication for your own product

slides.title: Real-Time Capture Beats Memory
bullets: Congress intelligence apps or simple shared templates enable live capture
Notes are timestamped, attributed, and instantly available to the team
The alternative is relying on memory or notes consolidated days later, once nuance is gone

slides.title: From Anecdotal Attendance to Collective Intelligence
bullets: Well-executed session tracking is systematic, not anecdotal
It converts individual attendance into actionable scientific intelligence
That intelligence serves the whole medical organization, not just the attendee

takeaway.title: Session tracking turns limited attendance into deliberate, team-wide coverage
bullets: Prioritize sessions before the congress, not while standing outside the room
Split coverage across the team and consolidate notes in one place
Structured, real-time notes beat memory every time
